key_insight: A qubit-efficient mapping for VQE can reproduce nuclear ground states with far fewer qubits, and the cSD mapping offers the best balance of resource efficiency and accuracy for mid p-shell nuclei.
engineering_relevance: The study shows how choice of qubit mapping directly affects circuit depth, qubit count, and error sensitivity, making it highly relevant for scalable quantum simulation of nuclear structure on near-term hardware.
method: Compare three qubit mappings: SD, cSD, and pnSD for shell-model nuclear Hamiltonians.
Run VQE circuits up to 26 qubits on a noisy simulator and IBM quantum hardware.
Evaluate ground-state energies and wavefunction fidelity for 10B and 12C.
evidence_signal: Hardware post-error-mitigated results gave 0.21% error for 10B with SD mapping, versus 3.37% for cSD and 8.88% for pnSD; for 12C, cSD was 6.82% from exact.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on the chosen mapping and error mitigation, so scalability to larger nuclei may still be limited by hardware noise and circuit resource growth.
paper_title: Qubit-efficient variational algorithm for nuclear structure
